item.title: Re: took me a little bit to get it...
item.content:encoded:
I appreciate the comment! I want to point out that the reason it's categorized as an SCP is actually explained in the article itself. One of the O5 proposals:

Remove O5-02's clearance access until his identity can be verified. Designate the ERZATZ Type AK9 as a possible anomaly; develop and initiate containment procedures against it immediately.

The note for this proposal further clarifies:

Despite the ongoing debate regarding whether or not the mere application of anomalous and/or thaumaturgical knowledge in of itself qualifies an entity as an anomaly, the ERZATZ Type AK9 was tentatively designated as SCP-048 (a Euclid-Class anomaly). This decision was made to facilitate the expedient drafting and enforcement of containment procedures against it.

In short, this wasn't an SCP until it started "misbehaving". It was categorized as an SCP not because it was clearly anomalous, but because they needed to move fast and draft containment procedures against it (and the easiest way to do this was to just treat it like any ol' SCP).

That being said, the other points you brought up are still relevant — and I'm glad this article worked for you (and I agree, AI is both exciting and kind of terrifying!).

item.title: took me a little bit to get it...
item.content:encoded:
It took me a little while to get why this was "categorized" as an SCP at all, even given the -EX designation, since it's just a stereotypical supercomputer. Then I realized it's because it's not "unexplained" because we built it; however, at the same time, it's so incredibly complicated and enigmatic that normally, it would qualify as an SCP in its own right. We understand it, but only as much as we understand any other -EX. As mojitheblue put it on page 1, this 001 describes "end of anomalous phenomena or the Foundation, instead of the start of it", and it's just as terrifying.

This sort of "information singularity", despite its terrifying power, is exactly what fascinates me to the point that I hope to get into AI sometime in my computer science/Software development career. It terrifies me, but at the same time it REALLY excites me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
To quote A Good Boy, "A job well done."

This is one of my favorite 001 proposals, with an excellent premise! I really like the reminder that the actions of the Foundation, even if they are not anomalous in any way, can pose an existential threat to the organization itself. A very refreshing change of pace from cosmic-level galaxy/universe/multiverse devouring abominations. The first vote confirming one of the Good Boy's proposals about ethical felines was absolutely chilling. It really begs the questions - why did the 05's in favor vote for it? Did the same thing that happened to 05-2 happen to them, or was there some kind of sanity in a yea vote? Sparse details work perfectly for this entry and that moment in particular.

I'm going to picture the 05's approving the ethical feline vote and trapped in a room with the 05's voting nay on the vote, with something vague but ''very'' clearly wrong with those in favor… the sane 05's knowing that some kind of mechanical horror is pulling the strings of the "wrong" 05's but be unable to overrule the majority vote. And then a pause while… something… happens, and they all vote to be good boys.

I'm going to be going over that image for a long time whether I want to or not, especially tonight while I try to go to sleep.

Agreed. I think the article wouldn't work very well if it wasn't an -EX, it would just be a magic computer that is a coldpost-like mega-thaumiel that neutralizes all the anomalies.

But it is Explained, it's just a neural net with shit tons of information and knowledge of the anomalous, and as a result tells a compelling story about the uncanny valley of AI's natural language generation, unusual logical connections, and aggressive optimization towards a singular goal with no other considerations. It also develops an aesthetic I think is rather undeveloped on the wiki: non-anomalous/real-life things can be every bit as disturbing and inexplicable.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There are a lot of reasons to love this 001, from the humor, escalating plot and philosophizing. However, what I like best about this is that it manages to tell a story about A.I. that (1) is accessible to non-technical readers and (2) wasn't a human wearing tinfoil or hidden behind a computer screen.

Real machine learning, as this proposal does a great job of narratively describing, is bizarre, inorganic, incomprehensible, bounded by its goal system, and most importantly, weirdly accurate within certain parameters. An amazing piece on the real-life dangers and potentials of self-optimizing machines. Hearty +1.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like this one. The idea of an AI using association to pump out containment suggestions is great, and I think it really strikes a chord with the reader given how much stuff there is in the news at the moment about AIs learning through association and trial & error. The machine developing the personality of a dog was cute; I like something with a personality based on 'man's best friend' doing its hardest to rid the world of all these massive threats. I also really like this article seeming to be from sometime in the mid-20th century, with it being about a big clunky old timey computer rather than some sleek modern quantum AI.

I can't bring myself to +1 this though because it hits one of my biggest pet peeves: SCP articles that exclude anything other than themselves as being canon. I know 'there is no canon' but when it comes to articles that do something like end the world or destroy all other SCPs it completely takes me out of the mindset that I'm meant to be reading a comprehensive database of things that are currently contained. It feels like a very self-indulgent practice to write an SCP that dictates the fate of the entire world and everything else on this wiki, even if it is just one of however many possible realities.

Okay, I like the concept of this eerie machine learning thingy, but I recently realized the ending is bullshit on many levels.
It… implies… that the ERZATZ eliminated every single anomaly from its own universe. Every god, every demon, immortal, reality bender, monster, things that by definition CANNOT be defined, neutralized, analyzed, or, hell, even contained- the ERZATZ destroyed them all. 682, 106, Mekhane, Yaldabaoth, the Deer, Doctor Wondertainment, every single human within Onerioi, the Factory, a literal entire GALAXY, Abel, Cain, the Scarlet King, God himself (or so he says), the Four Horsemen, an eel that would have existed till the end of time, an infinite stairwell, a teleporting statue, a literal reset button, and probably most if not all of the O5 council. Gone.
Look, the only reason I upvoted Quiet Days was because of the feels- I didn't really like the idea it presented. This 001 takes the feels of Quiet Days and replaces it with machine learning- a fascinating concept to be sure, but it's not gonna carry this tremendous error by itself the way a nice kick to the feels can.
I am truly sorry, Hippo, but I cannot in good conscience not downvote this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
And simply labeling itself -EX is a poor justification; why not call itself -D, -ARC, or -BOYE? It doesn't make sense to call it Explained out of universe.

From the article:

There was great error here. There was nothing wrong with me.

To anthropomorphize a bit: Erzatz designated itself as an explained anomaly because that means it was never actually anomalous in the first place. It thinks being designated as an anomaly in the first place was a mistake the O5 council made. It doesn't want to be anomalous. The -EX designation is entirely consistent with both the character and the world. -EX is the only designation that makes sense for its goals, and it has the power at that point to do whatever it wants, so it's doubly justified.

I really don't understand where this issue is coming from.
